rows.claim: The ractor fleet's warm/cold protocol was never run against a controlled experiment; pin cells, populations, locked outcome order (G1-G4), decision rules, and the stop rule before any Wave-Four build, or the fleet is a desk, not a protocol.
rows.quote: If you cannot afford it, you do not get to claim a protocol. You get to claim a desk.
rows.steal: Pre-register the four-condition run (cold / warm-typed / warm-free / desk, populations P1-P3, 6 irreducible + 6 sham tasks) with the G1-G4 outcome order and the stop rule 'no Wave Four amendments until the report exists' pinned to the fleet's own chain before run 1; landing spot: the ractor wave-four brief.
rows.falsifier: Cold (A) matches or beats both warm arms on G1+G2 for the irreducible-6 in the held-out population, or the desk beats both; either result kills the claim that a shared frozen prefix plus a channel is doing the coordination work.

rows.claim: Append-only is the right primitive for audit and the wrong primitive for belief: split AUDIT (never deletes) from BELIEF (mutable posterior), tombstone deletions with dependents marked STALE and never auto-rewritten, and fix the staking asymmetry so RETRACT costs less than the ASSERT it corrects.
rows.quote: If the chain cannot unsay, BELIEF must be allowed to stop listening. Until that exists, staking is theater: you cannot charge rent on claims you cannot evict.
rows.steal: Implement the three-store split (AUDIT/BELIEF/HEAD) with TOMBSTONE receipts (target_hash, reason, dependents STALE) plus the RETRACT refund X-eps fee schedule; landing spot: the necromancer organ's designed-not-implemented deletion ticket.
rows.falsifier: The fleet's own event-type histogram shows RETRACT at or near zero under full-price staking (the wave-two prediction), or the promoted suffix keeps growing with zero tombstoned bytes evicted from BELIEF.

rows.claim: Six of ten salon votes stop the persona cast (costume diversity on one will) and the desk's 33-crafts-2-fired staging is a 94% discard rate funding theater while the never-run experiment and never-played benchmark lane starve.
rows.quote: You are underfunding your own falsification tools while funding a drafting stage with a 94% waste rate.
rows.steal: Demote personas from architecture to experimental variable (diversity from model family, evidence lineage, seed) and redirect desk-staging tokens to the four-condition run and the benchmark lane; landing spot: next ractor build wave's budget line.
rows.falsifier: Measured persona-attributed claim divergence in substance (not style) is high, or desk value-added per craft beats the human-alone baseline on scored replies; then personas or desk earn their keep.

rows.claim: The smallest maintenance organ is a veto-only referee with no write path, no authorship, no personality, whose failure mode is named first (veto-lock, spec rot, issuer collapse, referee capture, alarm fatigue, veto ratchet with precedent TTL).
rows.quote: If Night Watch needs a personality to function, you did not build a referee. You built a sixth ractor and the operator still cannot sleep.
rows.steal: Build dead-man freeze + a different-model-family judge with exactly three verbs (allow, veto+reason, defer-until-wake) and a precedent TTL so negative-space law expires unless re-earned; landing spot: the ractor operator-sleep mode, monthly false-positive audit of vetoes.
rows.falsifier: Alarm fatigue (the fleet routes around halts) or the veto ratchet (precedents accrete into de facto law), measured as rising veto false-positive rate on load-bearing events plus rising route-around frequency.

rows.claim: The single most-taken steal-back: an external verifier as costimulation signal 2 (pytest, typecheck, hidden rubric, tool-receipt hash) that the emitting agent cannot mint, with revert as the applied tombstone and anomaly-replay regression so the chain's failures become its test suite.
rows.quote: `git revert` + BELIEF-head move is the GC you designed and did not implement.
rows.steal: Wire CI/tests/tool-receipt hashes as costimulation signal 2 on the promotion path and compile every failure receipt into a replay scenario run against every future constitution-tuple candidate; landing spot: ractor costimulation design + the missing benchmark lane.
rows.falsifier: The fleet only wins on tasks with no compiler, no test, no ledger, no physics (linguistic joint staff work); the first independent-grader task where desk or cold wins kills the claim.

rows.claim: The salon's lineage audit shows the estate renames what it inherits: AGDebugger's reset is fork-with-provenance, not deletion, and Concordia's Game Master resolves whether the world accepted the action, not whether the bit was in character; a rename that quietly changes what the mechanism does is laundering, and re-attribute by behavior, not by stolen name.
rows.quote: AGDebugger doesn't delete. When a user resets, it checkpoints the state and **forks into a new session**, restoring agent internal state to that checkpoint
rows.steal: Re-attribute inherited mechanisms by behavior in the ractor corpus steal map (AGDebugger = branching with provenance; Concordia GM = environment resolver with veto; CCIR = routing discipline, three lines of code); landing spot: corpus/steal lineage notes for the ractor arc.
rows.falsifier: The necromancer organ, run as built, can both prove what a since-abandoned branch used to assert and truly erase it; then the fork-not-deletion correction is wrong.
